svg.text: B-D FLACHBAND — a washable belt as the universal work surface
Items lie flat on a reversing belt and pass under a row of fixed stations; a retracting nose lays them gently into the pan.
900 W × 600 D × 550 H, belt top at 1150 mm
belt 300 × 800, homogeneous TPU, tooth-driven
12 axes · Schnitzel coverage > 95 % (est.)
wash box on the return strand: 3 min = 9 passes
SIDE VIEW along the belt

Close-up: the nose is a powered spatula (flip)
the 8 mm nose bar crawls under the item as the belt runs, lifts it, and lays it back turned over
curl belt turns it
pancake Ø 240 on a 300 mm belt: marginal; steaks, cutlets, fish: the main use
Close-up: belt dicer — strips along, then cuts across
top view: 14 circular gang knives (pitch 20, shifted 10 for a 2nd pass), then the guillotine
belt (top view), runs →
gang knives
guillotine
slabs come from a slicing disc at the dock chute; onions fall apart into rings → irregular dice
1/8 A cutlet is laid flat on the belt at the tail.
2/8 Under the sifter the belt runs forward and back: the cutlet is dusted with flour.
3/8 It passes through the egg curtain (25 g, fed by gravity from a spout lid).
4/8 Belt reverses: crumbs from the sifter, then the press roller sets them at 30 N.
5/8 At the end the nose retracts 150 mm under the cutlet: it is laid gently into the hot pan, not dropped.
6/8 Roulade: the press roller flattens the slice; mustard and filling are laid on, 20 mm bare edge in front.
7/8 The curl belt lowers onto the leading edge and runs backwards: the slice rolls up; the roll goes seam-down into the cassette.
8/8 Wash: the return strand runs through the wash box (scraper, spray bars at 55 °C, 82 °C final pass, air knife).
